data.name: Adhish
data.gender_notes: Adhish is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit root 'adh', meaning 'towards'. The name Adhish signifies the one who is the master or lord, ruling over a domain or an aspect of life. In Hindu mythology, Adhish is a name of various gods and goddesses, such as Adhish Shiva, the god of destruction, and Adhish Parvati, the goddess of love and fertility.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner master, the higher self that guides and rules over the individual's thoughts, emotions, and actions.
data.etymology: Adhish belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord, Master.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adhish total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Adhish was a legendary king of the Chandela dynasty in central India, ruling from around 1073 to 1110 CE. His reign marked a period of prosperity and expansion for the Chandela kingdom, which included the construction of the Hindu temple complex at Khajuraho.

Adhish is also mentioned in the epic poem 'Ramayana' as the name of a sage who helped the hero Rama in his quest to rescue his wife Sita from the demon king Ravana. In this context, Adhish is referred to as a wise and powerful ascetic who lived in the forest.
